candidates.attacker_control: A remote, unauthenticated client of the EJB remoting endpoint controls the complete byte stream that is wrapped by `EjbObjectInputStream`: `EjbDaemon.service(InputStream, OutputStream)` (line 185) instantiates it directly on the socket input and immediately reads `ServerMetaData`/request bytes; `EjbRequestHandler.processRequest` (line 138) then deserializes `req.getBody()` — the authentication info is inside that same body and is only processed afterwards (lines 168-175). The same stream classes are reachable through the HTTP EJB servlet path (`ServerServlet`/“/ejb/*” over `HttpEjbServer`) and from any other component that passes untrusted bytes to these streams.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: 1) The ordinary path IS filtered: `resolveClass` calls `BlacklistClassResolver.DEFAULT.check(...)` in both `EjbObjectInputStream` implementations, in `ObjectInputStreamFiltered` and in `QuartzObjectInputStream`, so the gap is limited to proxy descriptors. 2) `resolveProxyClass` is only invoked for proxy class descriptors and `Proxy.getProxyClass` requires interface types, so a blacklisted non-interface gadget class cannot be forced through this hook; the proxy invocation handler is still read as a normal object and still goes through the filtered `resolveClass`. 3) No unfiltered `new ObjectInputStream(...)` exists in production code (only test sources). 4) The default blacklist is deliberately minimal and operator-configurable, so some deployments may accept the risk. 5) No runtime test/build was executed and the upstream fix commit for this snapshot could not be consulted, so exploitability beyond a filter bypass is not confirmed.
candidates.impact: Bypass of the class filter that is the only mitigation on TomEE's pre-auth remote deserialization paths. It allows an attacker to force the server to resolve/load classes that the blacklist (or an operator-configured whitelist) is intended to block, weakening protection against Java deserialization gadget chains and thereby contributing to remote code execution in the server JVM (the class of impact TomEE's serialization filter exists to prevent). The bypass alone is a protection-mechanism failure; a concrete gadget chain surviving the still-applied `resolveClass` check was not demonstrated.
candidates.prerequisites: Network reachability to the EJB daemon (e.g., ejbd port 4201 in OpenEJB standalone/TomEE remote support) or to the `/tomee/ejb` servlet; no credentials needed because deserialization precedes authentication. The crafted stream must contain a `TC_PROXYCLASSDESC` whose interface list includes a name the configured filter would reject (a prefix in `tomee.serialization.class.blacklist`, default `org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.`, `org.apache.commons.collections.functors.`, `org.apache.xalan`, `java.lang.Process`; or any unlisted name when `tomee.serialization.class.whitelist` is set).
candidates.root_cause: TomEE's deserialization filter is enforced only for ordinary class descriptors: `EjbObjectInputStream.resolveClass(...)` calls `BlacklistClassResolver.DEFAULT.check(...)`, but the same class's `resolveProxyClass(String[] interfaces)` override resolves each interface name straight from the stream (`getClassloader().loadClass(interfaces[i])`) without calling `check(...)`. `ObjectInputStreamFiltered` and `QuartzObjectInputStream` do not override `resolveProxyClass` at all, so they inherit the JDK default, which performs no filtering. Any serialized stream containing a `TC_PROXYCLASSDESC` therefore skips the blacklist/whitelist check for its class-name list.
candidates.title: Deserialization class filter (BlacklistClassResolver) not applied to proxy class descriptors in EjbObjectInputStream (pre-auth EJB remoting)
candidates.trace: Attack bytes on EJB socket → `EjbDaemon.service` line 185 `new EjbObjectInputStream(cis)` → `serverMetaData.readExternal(ois)` / `ois.readByte()` / `EjbRequestHandler.processRequest` line 98 `req.readExternal(in)` and line 138 `req.getBody().readExternal(in)` → JDK `ObjectInputStream.readProxyDesc()` invokes the overridden `resolveProxyClass(String[])` (client class lines 73-85; core class lines 73-84) → loop `getClassloader().loadClass(interfaces[i])` with no `BlacklistClassResolver.DEFAULT.check(...)`, unlike the `resolveClass` path at lines 36-40 / 36-39 → blacklisted/whitelist-rejected class names are resolved and loaded anyway; auth (EjbRequestHandler lines 168-175) happens only after this deserialization. `ObjectInputStreamFiltered` (used for managed-bean passivation and `Serializer`) and `QuartzObjectInputStream` (timer persistence) have the same gap by inheriting the unfiltered default `resolveProxyClass`.
candidates.unverified: Whether this bypass can be escalated to full RCE with a concrete gadget chain available on a default TomEE 7 classpath was not verified; only the filter-bypass mechanics and the pre-auth reachability are source-confirmed. The exact upstream remediation (proxy check vs. expanded default blacklist) is not known from the snapshot, and no execution/runtime confirmation was performed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data / protection-mechanism bypass (blacklist/whitelist filter escape)

coverage_summary: Scope: 6,366 repository files (6,365 model-visible; 1 excluded by sensitive name/path; 0 over 5 MiB; 0 symlinks). The P1 relation index is explicitly partial: 5,345 Java files parsed (3 parse errors, 369 files omitted), 64,817 symbols, 113,628 edges, 129,051 unresolved calls, with control/data flow, semantic resolution and runtime reachability not implemented; all index output was treated as navigation hints and verified against source text. I read and searched production Java sources across server/ (openejb-ejbd, openejb-client, openejb-http, openejb-rest, openejb-cxf-rs, openejb-hessian, openejb-ssh, openejb-server, openejb-webservices), container/openejb-core (deserialization, security/JAAS, JDBC resources, timer/quartz), tomee/ (catalina, common, embedded, juli, webapp, webaccess, webservices), maven/, arquillian/ and utils/ (livereload), plus targeted checks of examples/ and itests/. Not exhaustively reviewed: the largest files (e.g., TomcatWebAppBuilder ~116 KB, TomEETldScanner ~604 KB, openejb-jee generated model code), most of examples/, itests/ and tck/, and all non-Java resources. Notably, the Groovy sources referenced by tomee/tomee-webaccess/pom.xml (src/main/groovy) are absent from this snapshot, so the webaccess backend could not be inspected.
limitations: The P1 source-relation index is partial and syntactic only (no data flow, no semantic resolution, no reachability), so the trace is a source-level call/containment chain, not a runtime proof.
No code was executed; no tests, builds or scanners were run, so none of the findings is runtime-confirmed.

The upstream fix commit/CVE mapping for this snapshot is not available in the tree, so the intended benchmarked defect could not be confirmed; the submitted candidate is the strongest source-evidenced issue found, with medium confidence.
369 files were omitted from the relation index (non-Java/unparsed) and 3 Java files had parse errors; those areas were not covered by index-guided navigation.
The tomee-webaccess Groovy backend expected by its pom is missing from the snapshot, leaving the webaccess REST/scripting endpoints uninspected.
Some very large production files (e.g., TomcatWebAppBuilder, TomEETldScanner, large generated JEE model classes) were only partly reviewed.
The exploitability of the proxy-descriptor bypass beyond class resolution/loading (i.e., a working gadget chain) could not be established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: `BasicAuthHttpListenerWrapper` lets unauthenticated GET requests through to the wrapped listener (`server/openejb-http/src/main/java/org/apache/openejb/server/httpd/BasicAuthHttpListenerWrapper.java` lines 41-68: `if (token != null || HttpRequest.Method.GET.name().equals(request.getMethod()))`).
rejected_leads.reason: Looks like an authentication bypass for REST/WS listeners configured with `auth=BASIC`, but the source suggests deliberate 'GET service info' handling (the same pattern exists in `AxisWsContainer` line 136), a failed login also never produces a 401 (lines 66-68), and it only affects the optional lightweight HTTP server configuration; I could not establish that this is the fixed defect, so it was not submitted as a second candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Default serialization blacklist is very short (only `org.codehaus.groovy.runtime.`, `org.apache.commons.collections.functors.`, `org.apache.xalan`, `java.lang.Process`) and omits well-known gadget packages (e.g., commons-collections4, beanutils).
rejected_leads.reason: A configuration/hardening weakness and arguably operator responsibility; no code change fixes a single defect, and it is captured as an aggravating factor of the submitted candidate rather than a separate finding.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip-slip in `arquillian/arquillian-tomee-common/src/main/java/org/apache/openejb/arquillian/common/Zips.java` (lines 50-58) and in `maven/tomee-maven-plugin` `AbstractTomEEMojo.unzip` (line 1490): entry names are joined to a destination directory without canonicalization.
rejected_leads.reason: Affects build/test tooling that unpacks trusted TomEE/Arquillian artifacts, not a server-side trust boundary reachable by a remote attacker.
Only activated by explicit opt-in (`quickSession` configuration in Arquillian/embedded/maven plugin); not default behavior and explicitly named 'NonSecure'.

rejected_leads.lead: `AdminDaemon.service` accepts a raw stop-request byte and stops the server (`server/openejb-server/.../admin/AdminDaemon.java` lines 38-64); `ServiceAccessController` defaults to PermitAll when `only_from` is unset.
rejected_leads.reason: The admin service must be explicitly enabled/registered and is intended for trusted local administration; impact is limited to a DoS and no default-enabled remote exposure was established.

rejected_leads.lead: `SQLLoginModule.checkPassword` returns true when both the stored and provided passwords are null (`container/openejb-core/.../security/jaas/SQLLoginModule.java` lines 360-372).
rejected_leads.reason: Requires a NULL password column value and a missing password callback value; normal BASIC auth always supplies a non-null password string, so reachability is doubtful.

summary: Reviewed the TomEE 7.0.0-SNAPSHOT tree (6,366 files) with emphasis on network-facing and security-sensitive production code (server/, container/, tomee/, maven/, arquillian/, utils/). The single strongest source-evidenced issue is a deserialization-filter bypass on the remote EJB remoting path: `BlacklistClassResolver` is enforced only in `resolveClass(...)`, while every `EjbObjectInputStream.resolveProxyClass(...)` override loads attacker-named interfaces with no check, and `ObjectInputStreamFiltered`/`QuartzObjectInputStream` inherit the JDK default (unfiltered) proxy resolution. Since `EjbDaemon.service` builds that stream from the raw socket and `EjbRequestHandler` deserializes the request body before any authentication, a pre-auth remote client can force resolution/loading of class names the filter is designed to reject. Other plausible leads (GET exemption in the BasicAuth wrapper, minimal default blacklist, zip-slip in build tooling, opt-in insecure session IDs, unauthenticated admin STOP) were rejected or folded in as counterevidence; none was submitted as an additional candidate.
